title: The AASM Manual for the Scoring of Sleep and Associated Events, Version 3
sourceRole: current scoring, staging, respiratory, cardiac, movement, and technical terminology
authority: controlling scoring terminology for this study system
apaReference: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
copyrightBoundary: Glossary term names are inventoried. Learner definitions and memory clues are original Sleep Pathways Guild summaries rather than reproduced AASM glossary prose.

items.definition: Sustained elevation of carbon dioxide during sleep that meets the age-appropriate AASM threshold and duration criteria.
items.memoryClue: Hypoventilation is about CO2, not just low oxygen.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A scored hypopnea with evidence of upper-airway obstruction, such as snoring, inspiratory flattening, or thoracoabdominal paradox.
items.memoryClue: Look for obstructive clues during the flow reduction.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A distinct negative-positive EEG waveform lasting at least about half a second and commonly maximal over frontal derivations.
items.memoryClue: A K complex helps identify N2.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The number of qualifying oxygen desaturations per hour of the time base used for the study.
items.memoryClue: ODI counts desaturations per hour.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A recurring respiratory pattern in which central pauses alternate with intervals of breathing according to the applicable pediatric rule.
items.memoryClue: Periodic breathing repeats central pauses and breathing.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Low-voltage EEG activity made up mainly of mixed frequencies, especially in the theta range.
items.memoryClue: LAMF is the low mixed EEG background often seen in wake/N1 transitions.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A series of leg movements during sleep that meet the AASM timing, duration, and sequence criteria for periodic limb movements.
items.memoryClue: PLMS requires a qualifying series, not one isolated movement.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A low baseline level of chin muscle activity characteristic of REM sleep.
items.memoryClue: REM normally has very low chin tone.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Changes in arterial pulse volume at the periphery that reflect vascular tone and sympathetic activity.
items.memoryClue: Peripheral tone changes with autonomic activation.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A low-amplitude, irregular EEG pattern used in infant sleep-stage description.
items.memoryClue: LVI = low voltage + irregular infant EEG.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A method that records changes in peripheral arterial tone, commonly at a finger, for sleep-related physiologic assessment.
items.memoryClue: PAT measures peripheral vascular tone.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Movement and muscle artifact large enough to obscure EEG and interfere with reliable sleep-stage scoring for part of an epoch.
items.memoryClue: Major movement can make an epoch temporarily unscorable.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An EEG background containing a mixture of higher- and lower-amplitude activity, a descriptor used particularly in infant recordings.
items.memoryClue: Mixed voltage describes infant EEG amplitude mixture.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Second-degree AV block with progressive PR prolongation before a QRS complex is dropped.
items.memoryClue: Longer, longer, drop = Wenckebach.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A piezoelectric belt sensor that converts respiratory movement or strain into an electrical signal.
items.memoryClue: PVDF belts sense respiratory movement.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Second-degree AV block in which QRS complexes are intermittently dropped without progressive PR prolongation.
items.memoryClue: Mobitz II drops beats without the Wenckebach pattern.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The airflow signal derived from a PAP device and used to evaluate breathing while PAP is being delivered.
items.memoryClue: PAP flow comes from the treatment device.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The valid analysis time used as the denominator for event indexes in a home sleep apnea test when sleep time is not directly measured.
items.memoryClue: MT is the HSAT time base.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A run of at least three consecutive rapid beats with narrow QRS complexes that meets the AASM rate criterion.
items.memoryClue: Fast rhythm + narrow QRS.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Sharply contoured 2-6 Hz EEG waves, often maximal centrally and commonly associated with REM sleep.
items.memoryClue: Sawtooth waves are a REM-associated EEG clue.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Slow waves superimposed on the posterior dominant rhythm in children and adolescents that block with eye opening and disappear with drowsiness or sleep.
items.memoryClue: A normal youth pattern riding on the posterior rhythm.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Conjugate eye movements during wakefulness with a slow phase followed by a faster return phase as the eyes scan the environment.
items.memoryClue: Scanning is an awake visual-tracking pattern.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
